graph.summary: Aspirin → Prostaglandin G/H synthase 1 → prostaglandin biosynthetic process → Thromboxane A2 → platelet aggregation → Myocardial Infarction

evidence.snippet: It acetylates Ser529 residue in cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and prevents thromboxane A2 (TXA2) formation from arachidonic acid (AA) in platelets.
evidence.explanation: Aspirin covalently acetylates Ser529 of platelet COX-1, irreversibly inhibiting its catalytic activity.

paper.title: New direct and indirect methods for the detection of cyclooxygenase 1 acetylation by aspirin; the lack of aspirin resistance among healthy individuals.

evidence.snippet: In cancer cells, ASA and IP1867B acted by inhibiting PGE2 and TXB2 generation via the acetylation of COX-2.
evidence.explanation: Aspirin (ASA) acetylates COX-2 at Serine 516, inhibiting its prostanoid-generating activity.

paper.title: Characterization of the acetylation of cyclooxygenase-isozymes and targeted lipidomics of eicosanoids in serum and colon cancer cells by the new aspirin formulation IP1867B versus aspirin in vitro.

evidence.snippet: All aspirin doses caused comparable % acetylation of platelet COX-1 at Serine 529 associated with similar profound inhibition of platelet-dependent thromboxane (TX)A2 generation ex vivo (serum TXB2) and in vivo (urinary TXM).
evidence.explanation: Catalytically intact COX-1 drives platelet prostanoid biosynthesis; its acetylation by aspirin suppresses thromboxane A2 (a prostaglandin-class product) generation.

paper.title: Optimizing aspirin dose for colorectal cancer patients through deep phenotyping using novel biomarkers of drug action.

evidence.snippet: In cancer cells, ASA and IP1867B acted by inhibiting PGE2 and TXB2 generation via the acetylation of COX-2.
evidence.explanation: COX-2 activity is required for PGE2 and TXB2 (prostaglandin biosynthetic) generation; acetylation of COX-2 by aspirin reduces it.

paper.title: Characterization of the acetylation of cyclooxygenase-isozymes and targeted lipidomics of eicosanoids in serum and colon cancer cells by the new aspirin formulation IP1867B versus aspirin in vitro.

evidence.snippet: It acetylates Ser529 residue in cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and prevents thromboxane A2 (TXA2) formation from arachidonic acid (AA) in platelets.
evidence.explanation: TXA2 is the platelet-specific prostanoid output of COX-1-mediated arachidonic acid metabolism (the prostaglandin biosynthetic process).

paper.title: New direct and indirect methods for the detection of cyclooxygenase 1 acetylation by aspirin; the lack of aspirin resistance among healthy individuals.

evidence.snippet: Exposing aspirin to erythrocytes blocked its ability to inhibit thromboxane A(2) synthesis and platelet aggregation.
evidence.explanation: Loss of inhibition of TXA2 synthesis tracks with loss of inhibition of platelet aggregation, consistent with TXA2 driving aggregation.

paper.title: Intracellular erythrocyte platelet-activating factor acetylhydrolase I inactivates aspirin in blood.

evidence.snippet: aspirin significantly reduced the risk of both, fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarction
evidence.explanation: Aspirin's inhibition of platelet aggregation translates to a reduction in MI risk, indicating platelet aggregation contributes to MI.

paper.title: [Milestones of cardivascular pharmacotherapy: salicylates and aspirin].
